A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACID/ACED research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, 27-task StableEval results, captioning and VQA evaluations, and scaling and sensitivity studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds an evaluated comparison with four alternative batch-selection methods in Appendix G, Table 6.

M1.justification: ACID's scoring and joint batch sampling, ACED's combined contrastive and distillation objectives, and the model architectures remain unchanged. The flexible-resolution scoring discussed in Appendix J is explicitly not implemented.

E1.justification: Training datasets, the 27 StableEval evaluations, and captioning/VQA coverage are retained. The new batch-selection comparison reuses DataComp-1B and existing evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix G substantially expands the comparison scope to competing online data selectors: Bad-Students, Selective-Backprop, RHO-Loss, and JEST. These receive explicit evaluated rows in Table 6; v1 cited these approaches without reporting this direct comparison. Existing KD and pretrained-model comparators remain.

E3.justification: Retained experiments keep their preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, metrics, and StableEval protocol. The added comparison uses the existing SigLIP/DataComp-1B setup with 3B samples seen. Appendix J introduces analytical cost accounting without reporting changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendix J adds a quantitative training-overhead analysis, combining per-iteration cost estimates with the retained Figure 9 scaling results and comparing costs with MobileCLIP. Existing model-size, teacher-data, objective, ensemble, and hyperparameter analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A retains the same five-seed evaluation-stability study, fixed data ordering, and standard-deviation aggregation. The added baseline table introduces no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports additional comparison results, including 27-task averages of 65.8 for ACID, 64.4 for JEST, and 62.6 for RHO-Loss. Appendix J adds derived cost estimates. Existing Tables 2–3 and the detailed per-dataset results, renumbered from Table 6 to Table 7, retain their values.

T1.justification: The core implicit-distillation mathematics and Appendix B–D derivations are unchanged. Appendix J adds a limited computational-cost derivation: under reference-embedding caching and filtering ratio 0.8, it derives per-iteration costs of 3(FI + FT) for IID training and 7(FI + FT) for ACID.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: active curation as implicit distillation, its complementarity with KD, and inference-efficient multimodal models. The new evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix J newly explains the training-versus-inference tradeoff, acknowledges training overhead, and argues that deployment can amortize training cost. It also discusses potential savings from unimplemented flexible-resolution scoring. Existing domain-transfer and device-latency limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G documents the reimplemented baselines' dataset, training budget, objective, and reference-model choice. Appendix J specifies caching and resource-accounting assumptions. Existing training hyperparameters, architectural details, and big_vision/JAX implementation information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set remains unchanged. Appendix G adds explicit empirical positioning against prior batch-selection methods, while Appendix J develops the training-cost comparison with MobileCLIP and discusses efficiency techniques from previously cited work.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose in the introduction, related work, and experimental discussion, replaces generic supplementary references with specific appendix references, and inserts Appendices G and J. The main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the batch-selection comparison table, renumbers the existing detailed-results table, and adjusts table captions and placement. Figure 1 changes the DatologyAI label and marker presentation; the remaining figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix G strengthens the evidence by directly comparing ACID with relevant alternative data selectors. Appendix J makes training overhead and its assumptions more explicit. These are useful, bounded improvements to an otherwise stable paper. The cost analysis remains conditional on cached reference embeddings and does not establish measured end-to-end training savings.
